title: Grade 10 Chemistry National Exam & Practice 2014 (4 Chapters Combined)
description: Comprehensive examination bank combining 4 chapters (100 questions). Official Ethiopian national curriculum.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is correct regarding alkenes and alkynes?
options: The molecules of alkenes and alkynes are held together by weak intermolecular force.
Alkynes have longer bond length and larger face area than alkenes.
Alkenes are soluble in polar solvents, while alkynes are not soluble in polar solvents.
Alkenes and alkynes are soluble in polar solvents.
questions.explanation:
Alkenes and alkynes are nonpolar hydrocarbons.

 Their molecules interact mainly through weak van der Waals (dispersion) forces.

 They generally have low solubility in polar solvents and do not have longer bond lengths compared to alkanes or each other in the way described in option B.

questions.questionText: What is the general formula of alkynes?
questions.explanation:
Alkynes are unsaturated hydrocarbons containing at least one carbon–carbon triple bond. 

Their general formula is CₙH₂ₙ₋₂, where n is the number of carbon atoms and n ≥ 2.

questions.questionText: Which of the following represents the general formula of monohydric alcohols?
questions.explanation:
Monohydric alcohols contain only one hydroxyl (-OH) group.

 Their general formula is CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH, where n is the number of carbon atoms.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statement is INCORRECT regarding the boiling points of alkanes?
options: The boiling point of cycloalkanes is higher than that of linear alkanes.
Boiling points of straight chain alkanes is greater than that of branched chain alkanes.
Surface area is the only factor that determines the boiling points of alkanes.
Boiling points increases with stronger Van der Waals forces.
questions.explanation:
The boiling point of alkanes depends on molecular size, surface area, and intermolecular forces (Van der Waals forces).

 While linear alkanes generally have higher boiling points than branched ones due to greater surface area, it is incorrect to say that surface area is the only factor.

 Cycloalkanes, branching, and molecular weight also affect boiling points.

questions.questionText: What is a Lewis acid? It is
questions.explanation: According to Lewis theory, a Lewis acid is a substance that can accept a pair of electrons to form a coordinate covalent bond, whereas a Lewis base donates an electron pair.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a polyprotic acid?
questions.explanation:
A polyprotic acid is an acid that can donate more than one proton (H⁺) per molecule.

 H₃PO₄ (phosphoric acid) can donate three protons, making it a triprotic acid. 

The other acids listed (HNO₃, HF, HCl) are monoprotic, donating only one proton each.

questions.questionText: Which of the following does represent a general property of a base?
options: Aqueous solution of bases turns methyl orange to red.
Soluble bases release hydronium ion in aqueous solution.
Aqueous solution of bases turns blue litmus paper to red.
Solutions of strong bases are good conductors of electricity.
questions.explanation:
Bases, especially strong bases, dissociate in water to produce hydroxide ions (OH⁻).

 This ionization allows the solution to conduct electricity. 

Other options are incorrect: bases turn red litmus blue, not the other way around; they do not release hydronium ions; and they turn methyl orange yellow, not red.

questions.questionText: What are salts? Salts are
options: ionic compounds formed by partial replacement of ionizable hydrogen by metal cations.
ionic compounds that derive their cations from a base and their anions from an acid.
ionic compounds that result from the reaction between metal hydroxide and water.
ionic compounds formed by complete replacement of ionizable hydrogen by anions of the acid.
questions.explanation:
Salts are ionic compounds formed when the hydrogen ion (H⁺) of an acid is replaced by a metal cation from a base. 

They consist of cations from a base and anions from an acid, and are usually formed during neutralization reactions.

questions.questionText: The process in which a compound absorbs electrical energy and decomposes into its elements is
questions.explanation:
Electrolysis is the process in which an electric current is passed through a compound (usually molten or in solution) causing it to decompose into its constituent elements.

 Examples include the decomposition of water into hydrogen and oxygen.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true about galvanic cells used in commercial lead storage batteries?
options: The galvanic cells are made up of PbO₂ of anodes.
Half of the galvanic cells are connected in series.
Galvanic cells are connected to parallel.
Galvanic cells are connected in series.
questions.explanation:
In commercial lead-acid batteries, multiple galvanic cells are connected in series to increase the total voltage output.

 Each cell consists of a lead (Pb) anode and lead dioxide (PbO₂) cathode in sulfuric acid electrolyte.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of synthetic cryolite in the extraction of aluminum by the Hall's process?
options: Cryolite is used as a catalyst in the extraction of aluminum.
Cryolite increases the melting point of alumina.
Cryolite reduces the melting point of alumina.
Cryolite increases the purity of the extracted aluminum.
questions.explanation:
In the Hall-Héroult process for extracting aluminum, alumina (Al₂O₃) has a very high melting point (~2072°C).

 Synthetic cryolite (Na₃AlF₆) is added to dissolve alumina and reduce its melting point to about 900°C, making electrolysis practical and energy-efficient.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a chemical property of aluminum?
options: Aluminum has a lower density than any other commercial metal.
Aluminum is a good conductor of heat and electricity.
Aluminum is a grey metal in color.
Aluminum liberates hydrogen gas from dilute acids like HCl and H₂SO₄.
questions.explanation:
Chemical properties describe how a substance reacts with other substances. 

Aluminum reacts with dilute acids such as HCl or H₂SO₄ to liberate hydrogen gas, which is a chemical reaction.

 The other options (A, B, C) describe physical properties, not chemical properties.

questions.questionText: How is tanning carried out? In tanning the hides or skins are
options: treated with dilute hydrochloric acid to remove the lime.
soaked in lime and water for several days.
soaked in water for several days.
questions.explanation:
Tanning is the process of converting raw hides or skins into leather, making them durable and less prone to decomposition. 

This is typically done by treating the hides with chromium salts (like chromium(III) sulfate), which cross-link the collagen fibers in the skin.

questions.questionText: Which metal is obtained by the reduction of its oxide with carbon?
questions.explanation: Iron is extracted from hematite by reduction with carbon in a blast furnace.

questions.questionText: Adding aqueous ammonia to a solution containing Cu^2+ ions results in the formation of a:
questions.explanation: The test for copper(II) ions involves adding aqueous ammonia, which initially forms a light blue precipitate of copper(II) hydroxide.

questions.questionText: Which type of reaction is 2Na + Cl₂ → 2NaCl?
questions.explanation: Two elements combine to form a compound, so it is a combination reaction.

questions.questionText: What will be the product if phosphorus reacts with excess amount of oxygen?
questions.explanation:
When phosphorus (P₄) reacts with excess oxygen, it forms tetraphosphorus decoxide (P₄O₁₀).

 If the amount of oxygen is limited, tetraphosphorus hexoxide (P₄O₆) is formed. 

H₃PO₃ and H₃PO₄ are acids that can be formed by dissolving these oxides in water, not by direct reaction of phosphorus with oxygen.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the product of fractional distillation of crude oil?
questions.explanation:
Fractional distillation of crude oil separates its components based on boiling points. 

Kerosene is one of the fractions obtained. Producer gas and water gas are manufactured gases, and naphthalene is obtained from coal tar, not from crude oil distillation.

questions.questionText: Which of the following would increase the solubility of O2 gas in water?
options: Decreasing the pressure of O2 above the water
Increasing the pressure of O2 above the water
questions.explanation: According to Henry's Law, the solubility of a gas in a liquid is directly proportional to the partial pressure of that gas above the liquid. Increasing the pressure forces more gas molecules into the solution.

questions.questionText: The process in which a substance loses electrons in a chemical reaction is _____.
questions.explanation: Loss of electrons is oxidation: OIL = Oxidation Is Loss.

questions.questionText: Which type of reaction occurs when an acid reacts with a metal to produce hydrogen gas?
questions.explanation: Metal displaces hydrogen from the acid; this is a single displacement reaction.

questions.questionText: For the reaction BaCl2(aq) + Na2SO4(aq) -> BaSO4(s) + 2NaCl(aq), what is the correct complete ionic equation?
questions.explanation: A complete ionic equation shows all soluble ionic compounds dissociated into their constituent ions. The insoluble precipitate, BaSO4, is written as a solid.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a characteristic property of a base?
options: Reacts with active metals to produce H2 gas
questions.explanation: Aqueous solutions of bases (alkalis) have a characteristic slippery or soapy feeling and a bitter taste. [cite_start]Acids have a sour taste. ]

questions.questionText: A student collected few lemon from his/her back yard, brought it to their class and prepared a lemon juice in a beaker. They got blue and red litmus papers from his/her teacher.and placed few drops of lemon juice both on the red and blue litmus papers. What will be their observation on the litmus papers?
options: The blue litmus paper as well as the red litmus paper will maintain their color.
The blue litmus paper and the red litmus paper will turn colorless.
The red litmus paper will turn to blue and the blue litmus paper will maintain its color.
The red litmus paper will turn red and the blue litmus paper will maintain its color.
questions.explanation:
Lemon juice is acidic due to the presence of citric acid. 

Acids turn blue litmus paper red but do not change the color of red litmus paper. 

Therefore, upon adding lemon juice, the blue litmus paper will turn red, while the red litmus paper remains red.

questions.questionText: Which of the following mixtures is considered a homogeneous mixture?
questions.explanation: A homogeneous mixture has a uniform composition throughout. Air is a mixture of gases (nitrogen, oxygen, etc.) that are evenly distributed, making its composition uniform.

questions.questionText: What is a homologous series? A homologous series comprises of a group of hydrocarbons, in which each member differs from the next by a
questions.explanation: Successive members differ by one methylene group, –CH₂–, while having the same general formula and functional group.

questions.questionText: Which concentration unit is independent of temperature?
questions.explanation: Molarity, normality, and percent by volume all depend on the volume of the solution, which changes with temperature. Molality is based on the mass of the solvent, which does not change with temperature.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following DOES NOT involve a chemical change during the formation of a new substance?
questions.explanation: Vaporization is a physical change: liquid → gas without forming a new substance.

questions.questionText:
A Table salt and an oil are added to pure water. After stirring for a while, the salt disappears but the oil floats on the surface of the water.
Which of the following statements is the CORRECT reason that explains this demonstration?
options: The oil is insoluble in non-polar solvent.
The salt is soluble in polar solvent.
The salt is soluble in non-polar solvent.
The oil is soluble in polar solvent.
questions.explanation:
Water is polar, so ionic salt dissolves in it.
 Non-polar oil does not dissolve in polar water.

questions.questionText: The IUPAC name of the compound with the following structure is:
questions.explanation: Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.

questions.questionText: Which factor primarily determines the physical state (gas, liquid, or solid) of an unbranched alkane at room temperature?
options: The length of the carbon chain (molecular mass)
questions.explanation: The physical state of hydrocarbons is primarily determined by the strength of intermolecular forces (London dispersion forces), which increase with increasing molecular surface area and **molecular mass** (chain length). Shorter chains are gases, medium are liquids, and long chains are solids.

questions.questionText: In the electrolysis of molten sodium chloride (NaCl), what product is formed at the cathode?
questions.explanation:
The cathode is the site of reduction. 
In molten NaCl, the only species available for reduction is Na+ (Na+ + e- → Na), forming sodium metal.

questions.questionText: The complete ionic equation for the reaction of HCl(aq) and NaOH(aq) is: H+(aq) + Cl-(aq) + Na+(aq) + OH-(aq) -> H2O(l) + Na+(aq) + Cl-(aq). What is the net ionic equation?
questions.explanation: The net ionic equation is derived by removing the spectator ions (Na+ and Cl-) from the complete ionic equation. This leaves the essential reaction, which is the formation of water from hydrogen and hydroxide ions.

questions.questionText: The thermal decomposition of magnesium nitrate, Mg(NO3)2, produces magnesium oxide, oxygen, and which other product?
questions.explanation: Nitrates of Group IIA metals like magnesium decompose on heating to produce the metal oxide (MgO), oxygen gas (O2), and nitrogen dioxide gas (NO2).

questions.questionText: In an exothermic reaction, how does the energy of the products compare to the energy of the reactants?
options: Products have lower energy than reactants.
Products have higher energy than reactants.
Products have the same energy as reactants.
questions.explanation:
An exothermic reaction releases heat energy to the surroundings, meaning the total energy contained within the chemical bonds of the products must be less than that of the reactants.
 The change in enthalpy (ΔH) is negative.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the correct procedure for safely diluting a concentrated acid?
options: Pour the water into the acid quickly
Pour the acid into the water slowly
Pour the water into the acid slowly
Mix equal volumes of acid and water simultaneously
questions.explanation: To dilute concentrated acids, one must pour the concentrated acid into water, never the other way around. This is because the dilution process is highly exothermic, and adding water to acid can cause it to boil and splatter.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is considered an alloy?
questions.explanation: An alloy is a solid solution of two or more metals, or a metal and a nonmetal. A dental filling made of mercury (a liquid) dissolved in silver (a solid) is an example of a solid solution.

questions.questionText: In the reaction: N2 + 3H2 → 2NH3. If 6 moles of H2 are completely reacted, what is the amount of heat involved compared to the standard enthalpy change of the reaction (ΔH)?
options: Three times the magnitude of ΔH
questions.explanation:
The balanced equation shows 3 moles of H2 reacting for the standard ΔH.
 Since 6 moles (twice the amount) are reacted, the total heat involved will be twice the standard enthalpy change.

questions.questionText: What is the mass percentage of a solution made by dissolving 20 g of NaOH in 80 g of water?
questions.explanation: Mass percentage = (mass of solute / mass of solution) x 100%. Mass of solution = 20 g NaOH + 80 g H2O = 100 g. So, (20 g / 100 g) x 100% = 20%.

questions.questionText: What is the main component of 'Chile saltpeter'?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen exists in nature in the form of compounds such as sodium nitrate, which is also known as Chile saltpeter (NaNO3).

questions.questionText: Potassium plays an essential role in plants by:
options: Controlling the turgidity of plant cells
Being a major component of proteins
questions.explanation: Potassium, absorbed as the K+ ion, is the most important ion in controlling the turgidity (stiffness due to water pressure) of plant cells and also helps regulate stomata movement.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of an efflorescent salt?
questions.explanation: Efflorescent salts are hydrated salts that lose their water of crystallization to the atmosphere. [cite_start]Hydrated sodium carbonate is a primary example.

questions.questionText: What is the pOH of a 0.001 M solution of KOH, a strong base?
questions.explanation: Since KOH is a strong base, it dissociates completely, so [OH-] = 0.001 M = 1 x 10^-3 M. The pOH = -log[OH-] = -log(10^-3) = 3.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a key use of common salt, NaCl?
options: In the manufacture of baking soda
questions.explanation: Sodium chloride (common salt) is a raw material for the manufacture of sodium, chlorine, sodium hydroxide, baking soda (NaHCO3), and washing soda (Na2CO3).

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true for the anode in an electrolytic cell?
options: It is the negative electrode and the site of reduction.
It is the positive electrode and the site of reduction.
It is the negative electrode and the site of oxidation.
It is the positive electrode and the site of oxidation.
questions.explanation: In an electrolytic cell, the anode is forced to be positive by the external power supply, and it is still the site where oxidation ('An Ox') occurs.

questions.questionText: The decomposition of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) to water and oxygen can be sped up by a catalyst such as:
questions.explanation: The decomposition of hydrogen peroxide is a slow reaction that can be catalyzed (sped up) by substances like manganese(IV) oxide (MnO2) or platinum (Pt).

questions.questionText: If a reaction causes a temperature drop in the surrounding environment, the reaction's change in enthalpy (ΔH) is:
options: Cannot be determined from the temperature drop.
questions.explanation:
A temperature drop in the surroundings means the system absorbed heat from the surroundings (endothermic reaction).

 The absorption of heat corresponds to a positive change in enthalpy (ΔH > 0).

questions.questionText: What type of salt is barium sulfate (BaSO4), which is used as a 'barium meal' for X-rays?
questions.explanation: Barium sulfate is famously insoluble in water and acids. This property allows it to coat the digestive tract for X-ray imaging without being absorbed into the body.

questions.questionText: Identify the oxidizing agent in the reaction: 2Na + Cl2 → 2NaCl.
questions.explanation: Chlorine (Cl2) changes from oxidation state 0 to -1 (gains electrons/is reduced), therefore it is the oxidizing agent.

questions.questionText: What is the oxidation number of chromium (Cr) in the dichromate ion (Cr2O72-)?
questions.explanation:
Let x be the oxidation number of Cr.
 The sum must equal the charge (-2). 2x + 7(-2) = -2. 2x - 14 = -2.
 2x = 12. x = +6.

questions.questionText: What is the final concentration of a solution prepared by mixing 100 mL of 0.2 M HCl with 100 mL of 0.4 M HCl? (Assume volumes are additive)
questions.explanation: Calculate total moles: (0.1 L x 0.2 M) + (0.1 L x 0.4 M) = 0.02 mol + 0.04 mol = 0.06 mol. Calculate total volume: 100 mL + 100 mL = 200 mL = 0.2 L. Final Molarity = total moles / total volume = 0.06 mol / 0.2 L = 0.3 M.

questions.questionText: Which factor must be considered when determining if a reaction is spontaneous in an electrochemical cell?
options: Sign of the standard cell potential (E° cell).
questions.explanation: A reaction is spontaneous (occurs naturally) if the standard cell potential (E° cell) is positive.

questions.questionText: Which metal is extracted using coke and limestone in a blast furnace?
questions.explanation: Iron is extracted from hematite using coke and limestone in a blast furnace.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a peroxide?
questions.explanation:
A peroxide is a compound containing the O₂²⁻ ion.

 Among the given options, calcium peroxide (CaO₂) contains the peroxide ion, whereas ZnO, FeO, and K₂O are normal oxides containing O²⁻ ions.

 Peroxides release oxygen upon decomposition and are strong oxidizing agents.

questions.questionText: What is the primary product when a basic anhydride like Na2O reacts with an acidic oxide like CO2?
questions.explanation: A basic oxide reacts with an acidic oxide to form a salt. In this case, Na2O + CO2 -> Na2CO3 (sodium carbonate).

questions.questionText: If the temperature of the surroundings increases during a chemical reaction, the reaction is:
questions.explanation: An increase in the temperature of the surroundings indicates that the system has released heat energy to the surroundings, which is the definition of an exothermic reaction.

questions.questionText: Which non-metal is a major component of TNT and explosives?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen is a key element in explosive compounds like TNT.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of an emulsion?
questions.explanation: An emulsion is a type of colloid where a liquid is dispersed in another liquid. Milk is a classic example, consisting of fat globules dispersed in an aqueous solution.

questions.questionText: A 'concentrated' acid is one that has a:
options: Relatively large amount of solute dissolved in the solvent
Small number of replaceable hydrogen atoms
questions.explanation: The term 'concentrated' describes the relative amount of acid present in a solution. [cite_start]A concentrated acid has a relatively large amount of solute dissolved in the solvent.

questions.questionText: What is the primary danger of inhaling even small amounts of chlorine gas?
options: It causes inflammation of the lungs and mucous membranes
questions.explanation: Chlorine gas is extremely poisonous. Inhaling it, even in small amounts, causes severe irritation and inflammation of the respiratory system.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is NOT a type of chemical reaction?
questions.explanation: Deposition is a physical change (gas → solid), not a chemical reaction.

questions.questionText: What distinguishes a strong acid from a weak acid?
options: The concentration of the acid solution
The number of hydrogen atoms in the molecule
The degree of dissociation in water
questions.explanation: The strength of an acid is determined by its degree of dissociation in an aqueous solution. [cite_start]A strong acid, like HCl, dissociates completely, while a weak acid, like CH3COOH, only partially dissociates.

questions.questionText: Anhydrous salt of which of the following can absorb water from the atmosphere but remains in the solid state?
questions.explanation: Anhydrous CuSO₄ absorbs moisture and forms CuSO₄·5H₂O while remaining solid.

questions.questionText: Which statement best describes the difference between a strong base and a concentrated base?
options: Strength refers to degree of ionization, while concentration refers to the amount of solute.
There is no difference; the terms are interchangeable.
questions.explanation: Strength (strong vs. weak) refers to how completely a base ionizes in solution. Concentration (concentrated vs. dilute) refers to the amount of base dissolved in a given volume of solution.

questions.questionText: If the volume of an ideal gas increases at constant pressure, the system:
options: Has a decrease in internal energy.
questions.explanation: When a gas expands (increases volume) against a constant external pressure, it is pushing the surroundings and performing work on them (w is negative in physics convention, or positive for the surroundings).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is an essential nutrient of plants?
questions.explanation:
Potassium (K) is an essential macronutrient for plants. 

It regulates osmotic balance, activates enzymes, and is important for photosynthesis and growth.

 Sodium, aluminum, and lead are not essential; lead is toxic, aluminum can be toxic at high concentrations, and sodium is only essential for some plants in trace amounts.

questions.questionText: Which metal is obtained by roasting its sulfide ore and then reducing with carbon?
questions.explanation: Zinc sulfide is roasted to zinc oxide and then reduced to zinc metal.

questions.questionText: Which three elements are considered primary mineral nutrients for plants and are often found in complete fertilizers?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium are the primary mineral nutrients required by plants in relatively large amounts. [cite_start]Fertilizers containing these three elements are described as NPK fertilizers.

questions.questionText: What is the maximum oxidation number for a Group 1A metal element, such as Potassium (K)?
questions.explanation: Group 1A metals have a single valence electron, which they readily lose to form a stable cation with a charge of +1.

questions.questionText: Henry's Law states that the solubility of a gas in a liquid is directly proportional to the:
options: partial pressure of the gas above the liquid.
questions.explanation: Henry's Law describes the relationship between gas solubility and pressure. It states that C = kP, where C is the concentration (solubility) of the gas and P is its partial pressure.

questions.questionText: Which non-metal exists as diatomic molecules under normal conditions?
questions.explanation: Chlorine exists as Cl₂ molecules.

questions.questionText: A solution of H3PO4 is found to be 0.3 M. What is its normality if it reacts to form HPO4^2-?
questions.explanation: N = M x z. When H3PO4 reacts to form the hydrogen phosphate ion, HPO4^2-, it loses two of its three hydrogen ions. Therefore, z = 2. Normality = 0.3 M x 2 = 0.6 N.

questions.questionText: Which of the following salts is used in the treatment of waste water?
questions.explanation:
Ferric chloride (FeCl₃) is commonly used as a coagulant in water and wastewater treatment.

 It helps **remove suspended solids, colloids, and impurities** by forming flocs that can be easily separated. 

CaCO₃ is used for neutralization, BaSO₄ is insoluble and used as a pigment or contrast agent, and KNO₃ is a fertilizer.

questions.questionText: In the fractional distillation of crude oil, which fraction is typically collected at the highest temperature?
questions.explanation: Bitumen (asphalt) is the heaviest and highest boiling point residue remaining at the bottom of the fractional distillation column, while gasoline, kerosene, and naphtha are much lighter fractions collected at lower temperatures.

questions.questionText: Which of the following describes a supersaturated solution?
options: solution that can still dissolve more solute.
solution containing less solute than the saturation point.
solution containing more dissolved solute than a saturated solution at the same temperature.
solution in equilibrium with undissolved solute.
questions.explanation: A supersaturated solution is an unstable solution that contains a higher concentration of solute than is normally possible at a given temperature. It is usually created by cooling a saturated solution.

questions.questionText: Which property of metals allows them to reflect light?
questions.explanation: Metals are lustrous and have a shiny appearance due to reflection of light.

questions.questionText: Which is an example of a displacement reaction?
questions.explanation: Zinc displaces copper from copper sulfate, which is a displacement reaction.

questions.questionText: Which term is used to describe the half-cell where the electrode increases in mass in a galvanic cell?
questions.explanation:
At the cathode, reduction occurs (metal ions gain electrons and deposit as metal atoms).

 The formation of solid metal on the electrode causes its mass to increase.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a chemical change?
questions.explanation: Rusting of iron is a chemical change because it forms a new substance (iron oxide).

questions.questionText: Which of the following metals reacts vigorously with water?
questions.explanation: Sodium reacts vigorously with water to form hydroxide and hydrogen gas.

questions.questionText: Which is a double displacement reaction?
questions.explanation: Ag⁺ and Na⁺ exchange ions with Cl⁻ and NO₃⁻; it’s a double displacement.

questions.questionText: Which of the following compounds exhibits geometric (cis-trans) isomerism?
questions.explanation: Geometric isomerism requires restricted rotation (C=C double bond) and two different groups attached to each carbon of the double bond. In 2-butene, each C of the double bond is attached to a methyl group and a hydrogen atom, allowing for cis and trans forms.

questions.questionText: The common household substance vinegar contains which acid?
questions.explanation: Vinegar is a dilute solution of acetic acid (CH3COOH), which gives it its characteristic sour taste and pungent smell.

questions.questionText: What is the standard oxidation number of oxygen in most compounds, such as H2O and CO2?
questions.explanation:
In most compounds, the oxygen atom is more electronegative and gains two electrons, resulting in an oxidation number of -2.

 Exceptions include peroxides (-1) and compounds with fluorine (+2).

questions.questionText: A substance that facilitates the oxidation of another substance is called a(n):
questions.explanation: An oxidizing agent causes oxidation by itself undergoing reduction (gaining electrons).

questions.questionText: The negative logarithm of the molar concentration of hydrogen ion to the base ten is known as
questions.explanation:
The pH of a solution is defined as the negative logarithm (base 10) of the hydrogen ion concentration: pH = -log₁₀[H⁺].

 Kₐ is the acid dissociation constant, 

- pOH measures hydroxide ion concentration, 

- K_w is the ionization constant of water.

questions.questionText: Which reaction is endothermic?
questions.explanation: Decomposition of CaCO₃ absorbs heat.

questions.questionText: Which reaction is exothermic?
questions.explanation: Formation of water releases energy; exothermic reaction.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statement is CORRECT about metallic and electrolytic conductivity?
options: Both metallic and electrolytic conductivity is caused by the movement of highly delocalized electrons.
Electrolytic conductivity is caused by the movement of electrolytes, while metallic conductivity is caused by movement of ions.
Electrolytic conductivity is caused by the mobility of ions, while metallic conductivity is caused by movement of delocalized electrons.
Electrolytic conductivity is caused by the flow of mobile electrons, while metallic conductivity is caused by the movement of ions.
questions.explanation: Electrolytic conduction occurs by moving ions, while metallic conduction occurs through delocalized electrons.

questions.questionText: Molecular mass of H₂O is:
questions.explanation: H₂O has 2 H (2×1) + 1 O (16) = 18 g/mol.

questions.questionText: Which of the following processes is typically classified as an endothermic change?
options: Melting of ice at 0 degrees Celsius.
Rusting of iron in moist air.
Neutralization of an acid by a base.
questions.explanation:
Melting (solid to liquid) requires energy input (heat) to break intermolecular forces, making it an endothermic process.
 Combustion, rusting, and neutralization are all exothermic processes that release heat.

questions.questionText: Which non-metal exists as tetrahedral P₄ molecules in its white form?
questions.explanation: White phosphorus exists as P₄ tetrahedral molecules.

questions.questionText: Which shows reduction?
questions.explanation: Copper gains electrons to form Cu; reduction occurs.

questions.questionText: Which of the following best describes a mixture of sand and water?
questions.explanation: A suspension is a heterogeneous mixture in which solid particles are spread throughout a liquid without dissolving. The sand particles are large enough to be visible and will settle over time, which are key characteristics of a suspension.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a redox reaction?
questions.explanation: Zinc is oxidized and copper is reduced; both oxidation and reduction occur.

questions.questionText: The energy stored within the chemical bonds of a substance is known as its:
questions.explanation: Internal energy (U or E) includes the potential energy stored in chemical bonds and the kinetic energy of the particles.

questions.questionText: Which of these statements correctly compares molarity and molality for a dilute aqueous solution?
options: Molarity is always greater than molality.
Molality is always greater than molarity.
There is no relationship between them.
questions.explanation: For a dilute aqueous solution, the volume of the solution in liters is very close to the mass of the solvent (water) in kilograms because the density of water is approximately 1 kg/L and the volume of the solute is negligible. Thus, molarity (mol/L solution) and molality (mol/kg solvent) are nearly the same.

questions.questionText: In an electrochemical cell, the overall chemical reaction that occurs is typically a:
questions.explanation: All electrochemical processes, whether spontaneous (galvanic) or non-spontaneous (electrolytic), involve the transfer of electrons, making them redox reactions.

questions.questionText: Which process is responsible for dissolved solute returning to the solid state in a saturated solution?
questions.explanation: In a saturated solution, a dynamic equilibrium exists where the rate of dissolution (solute dissolving) is equal to the rate of recrystallization (dissolved solute returning to the solid phase).

questions.questionText: Which non-metal is used to make fertilizers and explosives?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen is used in the production of ammonia for fertilizers and in explosive compounds like TNT.
